evidence.source: Shuowen.org, 《說文解字》 entry with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry defines 房 as a room beside the main room (室在㫄也) and analyzes it as 从戶方聲. Duan Yucai glosses the left and right rooms in a hall as 房 and notes an extended use for a compartment of a ritual vessel. This is the received lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the character’s first formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「房」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.text: The page labels its displayed historical-form categories 楚系簡帛文字, 小篆, and 說文, and states that 戶 is the semantic element and 方 the phonetic element. The page’s glyphs are presented as images; I did not visually inspect them, so I cannot describe their stroke-level changes.
evidence.title: 漢字「房」：字形演變

evidence.source: Guoxuedashi character-form entry (search result; page open failed)
evidence.field: reported earliest graphic attestation and graphic development
evidence.text: The search result reports 房 first appearing in Warring States writing, with later Warring States, seal, clerical, and regular forms retaining 戶 plus 方. It also reports that some Chu manuscript forms add a short stroke above 戶. Because the page could not be opened, these details are treated as unverified leads rather than inspected evidence. The result’s proposed semantic contribution of 方 meaning ‘side’ is secondary speculation; the Shuowen analysis identifies 方 as phonetic.
evidence.title: 房字形演变字源_汉字「房」

evidence.text: The search result states that the graph first appears in Warring States writing. This supports a cautious reported terminus for presently identified forms, not proof that no earlier form existed. Earlier spoken use is not thereby excluded.
evidence.title: 房字形演变字源_汉字「房」

evidence.source: Wiktionary 房 entry, reporting Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang reconstructions
evidence.field: phonetic component and character historical pronunciation
evidence.text: Reported Old Chinese reconstructions for 房 are Baxter–Sagart *[Cə-N-]paŋ and Zhengzhang *baŋ; the same entry describes 房 as semantic 戶 plus phonetic 方, for which it reports Baxter–Sagart *paŋ / *baŋ and Zhengzhang *baŋ. In Middle Chinese transcription the entry gives 房 bjang and 方 bjang for the relevant readings, with 房’s Guangyun fanqie 符方切. These are reconstructions/transcriptions in named systems, not direct recordings of Old Chinese pronunciation. The approximate correspondence supports 方’s phonetic role; whether 方 also contributed ‘side’ is not established by these sound data.
evidence.title: 房 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary 方 entry, historical phonology table
evidence.text: The table gives 方 with Middle Chinese pjang for its ordinary reading and bjang for a separate reading matching 房’s Middle Chinese category; it reports Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[Cə-N-]paŋ / *paŋ and Zhengzhang *paŋ for the ordinary reading, and *baŋ for the reading corresponding to 房. This displays the variant scope relevant to comparison and cautions against quoting one reconstruction as the unique pronunciation of 方.
evidence.title: 方 - 維基詞典

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Revised Mandarin Dictionary
evidence.field: modern senses and cited literary examples
evidence.text: The entry lists 房 as ‘dwelling/house’, ‘a room within a dwelling’, house-like structures, family branches, and spouse/concubine senses. It cites Cao Pi’s Three Kingdoms-era poem 燕歌行 with 空房 (‘empty room’), and later medieval and imperial-era examples for other senses. These examples attest uses by their cited literary periods, but the dictionary list alone does not establish a chronological chain of semantic change.
evidence.title: 《重編國語辭典修訂本》房

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project search result, Taiping Yulan entry citing earlier texts
evidence.text: The search result quotes the Maoshi poem 君子陽陽: 左執簧，右招我由房, and a 尚書大傳 passage mentioning 至于房中. These are reported citations in a later compiled anthology and search snippets; I could not open the source page. They indicate early textual contexts for 房, but the exact dating and sense of 由房 remain interpretively disputed, so they do not securely date a particular semantic extension.
evidence.title: 太平御覽：居處部十三：房

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project search result, 毛詩類釋
evidence.field: interpretation of early phrase 由房
evidence.text: A search result gives a later commentator’s discussion of 君子陽陽’s 由房, including the interpretation of passing through a room toward an inner sleeping chamber and competing explanations linked with 房中 music. Since the page failed to open and these are later interpretations, the phrase’s original sense remains uncertain here.
evidence.title: 毛詩類釋：卷十二

gaps: No directly inspected ancient glyph image; the Academia Sinica form labels and searchable text do not permit a stroke-level description. The Warring States first-graphic-attestation claim comes from an inaccessible search-result snippet and needs confirmation from a readable paleographic catalogue or primary manuscript publication.

No dated inscription or manuscript containing 房 was directly inspected, so graphic chronology and any possible graphic corruption remain unresolved. There is no evidence here for a corruption/reanalysis event.
The early phrase 由房 has competing interpretations; the source containing the poem was not directly opened, and its exact sense should not be fixed from later commentary snippets.

The earliest attested senses cannot be securely ordered from the retrieved gloss lists. A traditional Shuowen gloss identifies a side room; later sources document room/house and other extensions, but do not establish every semantic link or their dates.

The evidence supports 方 as a phonetic element in 房. The possible additional semantic contribution ‘side’ is a secondary proposal, not independently demonstrated by the retrieved primary dictionary source.

Reported Sino-Tibetan comparisons (Tibetan and Burmese) appear in the Wiktionary entry, but I did not independently verify cognacy or chronology; they should not be presented as established etymology.

Modern pinyin fáng and Cantonese Jyutping fong4 are reported in the opened 房 entry, but the research did not independently consult authoritative pronunciation dictionaries for a complete modern-reading inventory.
